key_insight: The linear Poisson source for wall pressure stays inner-scale O(1) at very high Reynolds number, so the logarithmic growth of wall-pressure variance must come from the nonlinear source term.
engineering_relevance: This clarifies which turbulence mechanism drives high-Re wall-pressure levels, improving prediction models for aeroacoustics, boundary-layer loading, and surface pressure statistics.
method: Used simultaneous velocity and velocity-gradient hot-wire data from a single eight-sensor probe.
Compared a zero-pressure-gradient turbulent boundary layer with a high-Re pipe flow.
Examined inner-scaled factors in the linear pressure-source term and their Reynolds-number collapse.
evidence_signal: Measurements up to friction Reynolds numbers of order 10^4 show collapse of the linear-source factors and an inverse wall-distance decay of the relevant inertial-layer velocity-gradient variance.
watch_item: The conclusion is based on specific hot-wire datasets and inferred source-term decomposition, so extending it to other wall-bounded flows or extreme conditions still needs verification.
paper_title: An Inner-Scaled Linear Contribution to Wall-Pressure Variance at High Reynolds Number
